source.title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity

accepted.question_text: Given an asymptotically flat initial data set (M, g, K) in mathematical relativity and a future trapped surface Sigma, must there exist a smooth spherical apparent horizon outside Sigma, and must there also exist an apparent horizon inside Sigma?

evidence.quote: Given an asymptotically flat (AF) initial data set (M,g,K) and a (future) trapped surface L (i.e. tr:E(K+k) ~ 0), (a) show there is a (smooth, spherical) apparent horizon outside 2:. (b) show there is an apparent horizon inside :E.

accepted.question_text: To what extent is the analogy between apparent horizons and minimal surfaces valid, including whether a meaningful second-variation or stability theory for apparent horizons exists even though no functional is known whose Euler-Lagrange equations are the apparent-horizon equations?

evidence.quote: To what extent is this analogy valid? Unlike the area functional and minimal surfaces, there is no known functional for which the apparent horizon equations arise as the Euler-Lagrange equations. Does the "second variation" formula for apparent horizons mean anything?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist an asymptotically flat vacuum initial data set, diffeomorphic to R3, that contains an apparent horizon?

evidence.quote: Prove there is an AF vacuum initial data set, diffeomorphic to R3, which contains an apparent horizon.

accepted.question_text: Does there exist an asymptotically flat metric on R3 with zero scalar curvature that admits a minimal 2-sphere, and can such a minimal 2-sphere be stable; alternatively, can one prove that no such metric exists?

evidence.quote: Find an AF metric on R3 with zero scalar curvature and admitting a minimal 2-sphere, or prove there is no such metric. This is the previous question, but requiring a time-symmetric initial data set. Can the 2-sphere be a stable minimal surface?

accepted.question_text: Does an apparent horizon persist under Einstein evolution, or can one give an explicit counterexample; under what spacetime conditions can a trapped surface be extended indefinitely to a spacelike 3-cylinder of trapped surfaces with non-increasing area?

evidence.quote: Does an apparent horizon persist under the Einstein evolution? This is probably false, but I don't know of an explicit counterexample. An argument giving spacetime conditions under which a trapped surface can be indefinitely extended to a spacelike 3-cylinder of trapped surfaces, of non-increasing area, is given in [IW2].

accepted.question_text: For a conformally flat asymptotically flat metric g = phi^4 delta with non-negative scalar curvature, what conditions on the conformal factor phi guarantee that g has no horizon?

evidence.quote: Let· g = <p40 be a conformally flat, AF metric, with non-negative scalar curvature, so dcp ~ 0. Find conditions on cp which ensure g has no horizon.

accepted.question_text: If M is an asymptotically flat 3-manifold with non-negative scalar curvature and Sigma is a stable minimal 2-sphere in M, can one prove the Penrose inequality area(Sigma) <= 16 pi (ADM mass)^2, and can this inequality be generalized to initial data sets that are not time symmetric?

evidence.quote: Let M be a 3-manifold, AF with non-negative scalar curvature, and let :E c M be a stable minimal2-sphere. Prove the Penrose inequality [PRl] area(:E) ~ l61t (mass)2 where mass is the ADM mass of M. This would give an upper bound on the area of an apparent horizon in a time-symmetric data set. Find a generalisation of this inequality to initial data sets which are not time-symmetric.

accepted.question_text: For a compact 3-manifold M and conformal data (gamma_ab, A_cd, tau) used in the Lichnerowicz-Choquet-Bruhat-York system, where gamma_ab is a Riemannian metric, A_cd is traceless, divergence-free, and symmetric, and tau is the mean curvature, what conditions guarantee solvability when tau is not constant?

evidence.quote: Determine conditions on (Yab• A,cd, 't) which ensure the LCBY system is solvable, forM compact and 't non-constant (the constant-'t argument should generalise if I Vlog't I is sufficiently small).

accepted.question_text: What asymptotic conditions allow the conformal method to construct initial data sets on asymptotically hyperbolic manifolds, such as constant-mean-curvature hypersurfaces meeting future null infinity, also called hyperboloidal initial data sets?

evidence.quote: Describe suitable asymptotic conditions which enable the conformal method to be used to construct initial data sets on an asymptotically hyperbolic manifold (eg. a CMC hypersurface meeting ~+). Such initial data sets are called hyperboloidal.

accepted.question_text: Which hyperboloidal initial data arise from spacetimes with smooth conformal null infinity, and what class of Lichnerowicz-Choquet-Bruhat-York conformal data (gamma_ab, A_cd, tau) constructs such hyperboloidal initial data?

evidence.quote: Characterise those hyperboloidal initial data arising from a spacetime with a smooth conformal null infinity. Describe a class of LCBY data (Yab• A,cd, 't) which can be used to construct such hyperboloidal initial data.

accepted.question_text: What smoothness properties can hyperboloidal initial data have at a possibly generalized conformal infinity, and what are the weakest such conditions under which positivity of the Bondi mass can be proved?

evidence.quote: Classify the various kinds of smoothness properties which hyperboloidal initial data may have at (a possibly generalised) conformal infinity. In particular, find the weakest conditions under which a proof of positivity of the Bondi mass can be completed.

accepted.question_text: Can the space of globally hyperbolic vacuum Einstein metrics on V = R x M3 have more than one connected component, and what compactness or Palais-Smale-type condition for the mass function would be needed to analyze this question in the asymptotically flat setting?

evidence.quote: Can the . space of (globally hyperbolic, vacuum) Einstein metrics on V = RxM3 have more than one connected component? Gromov-Lawson [GL] have shown that the space of positive scalar curvature metrics on S7 does have more than one component (in fact, there are infinitely many components [CR]). It is known [CBM] that the mass function on 'f'JTI. (the set of maximal AF initial data sets satisfying the conditions of the positive mass theorem [BR6]) has only one smooth critical point, at R3. This suggests there is only one component in the space of AF spacetimes admitting a maximal Cauchy surface. What is needed here is some compactness/Palais-Smale condition for the mass function on 'U" 'JTI..

accepted.question_text: What conditions on the stress-energy tensor are sufficient to prove that a static asymptotically flat metric is spherically symmetric, in particular in the conjectural case that a static star is spherically symmetric?

evidence.quote: What conditions on the stress-energy tensor are needed to show that a static, AF metric is necessarily spherically symmetric? For perfect fluid stress-energy, this is the conjecture that a static star is spherically symmetric.

accepted.question_text: Can one give a good local characterization of the Kerr solution among stationary metrics, preferably one that does not depend on the slicing used?

evidence.quote: Find a "good" local characterisation of the Kerr solution amongst stationary metrics (preferably independent of the slicing used).

accepted.question_text: If two disjoint Cauchy surfaces in an asymptotically flat vacuum spacetime are isometric as initial data, must the spacetime be stationary, meaning that it admits a timelike Killing vector field?

evidence.quote: Suppose (Mi,gi,Ki), i=l ,2, are disjoint Cauchy surfaces in an AF (vacuum) spacetime, which are isometric (Le. there is a map ~p:M -?M , such that <p*g2 = g1 , l([l*K2 = K1 ). Show that the spacetime is stationary (admits a timelike Killing vector field).

accepted.question_text: What singularities can occur in solutions of the static and stationary vacuum Einstein equations, beginning with the possible singularities of the spacelike slices?

evidence.quote: Give a general discussion of the possible types of singularities which may occur for solutions to the static and stationary vacuum Einstein equations, starting with a description of the possible singularities of the spacelike slices.

accepted.question_text: Can one prove existence of the non-singular, asymptotically flat, static, spherically symmetric Einstein-Yang-Mills solutions that had been observed numerically?

evidence.quote: Recently it has been shown numerically that the static, spherically symmetric Einstein-Yang-Mills (EYM) equations have non-singular, AF solutions [BM]. This raises many interesting questions, for example: (i) prove existence of the static spherically symmetric EYM solutions;

accepted.question_text: Can one prove that there is no static spherically symmetric Einstein-Yang-Mills solution with non-zero electric field?

evidence.quote: (ii) show there is no static spherical solution with non-zero electric field;

accepted.question_text: Can one analyze the time-dependent spherically symmetric Einstein-Yang-Mills equations, in analogy with the analysis of spherically symmetric Einstein-scalar-field equations?

evidence.quote: (iii) analyse the time dependent spherically symmetric equations, analogous to the analysis of the spherically symmetric Einstein-scalar field equations in [CD2];

accepted.question_text: Are there axially symmetric static or stationary Einstein-Yang-Mills solutions that generalize the Kerr-Newman solution?

evidence.quote: (iv) find axially symmetric static or stationary solutions generalising the Kerr-Newman solution;

accepted.question_text: Is there an Einstein-Yang-Mills analogue of the Majumdar-Papetrou superposition of extremal Reissner-Nordstrom solutions?

evidence.quote: (v) find an EYM generalisation of the Majumdar-Papetrou superposition of extremal RN solutions [HH];

accepted.question_text: Can one prove that every static black-hole solution of the Einstein-Yang-Mills equations is Reissner-Nordstrom?

evidence.quote: (vi) show that a static black hole solution of EYM must be Reissner-Nordstr!llm (An EYM black hole has no YM hair [YP;GE]).

accepted.question_text: Can one prove an approximation theorem for the vacuum Einstein equations: if an approximate metric g_epsilon has Ricci curvature bounded by epsilon in a suitable norm, then there exists an exact Ricci-flat metric g within epsilon of g_epsilon in a suitable norm?

evidence.quote: Prove any result of the form: Conjecture: Let ge be an "approximate solut~on" of the (vacuum) Einstein equations (i.e. IIRic(ge)ll :s; e, in some suitable norm). Then there is a metric g such that Ric(g) = 0 and Ug-gell :S: e .

accepted.question_text: Can one show that any solution of the Einstein equations linearized about Minkowski space is close to a non-flat exact solution of the full Einstein equations?

evidence.quote: Show that a solution of the linearised Einstein equations (linearised about Minkowski space) is close to a (non-flat!) exact solution.

accepted.question_text: Under what precise conditions do post-Newtonian and post-Minkowskian asymptotic expansions converge, or at least approximate a global solution of the Einstein equations, possibly over a non-flat background metric?

evidence.quote: Show precise conditions under which the post-Newtonian and post-Minkowskian expansions converge, or at least approximate, a global solution. It may be necessary to work with a non-flat background metric.

accepted.question_text: Can one prove the existence of a limiting regime in which solutions of the Einstein equations reduce to Newtonian spacetimes?

evidence.quote: Prove the existence of a limit in which solutions of the Einstein equations reduce to Newtonian spacetimes.

accepted.question_text: Can one find a simple, usable approximation scheme that accurately determines the gravitational radiation from an isolated astrophysical system, and in particular can one prove the quadrupole radiation formula?

evidence.quote: Find a simple, usable approximation scheme which allows one to determine (accurately) the gravitational radiation produced by an isolated astrophysical system. In particular, prove the quadrupole radiation formula.

accepted.question_text: Can one show that test particles, modeled as very small but finite bodies, move along spacetime geodesics?

evidence.quote: Show that test particles (very small, but finite, bodies) move on spacetime geodesics.

accepted.question_text: In what sense does a Regge spacetime, described as a piecewise linear manifold with a piecewise linear metric given by edge lengths, approximate a smooth vacuum spacetime, and how should analogous convergence questions be formulated for numerical relativity spacetimes?

evidence.quote: In what sense does a Regge spacetime [RT],[BrL] - a piecewise linear (PL) manifold with PL metric (=leglengths) - approximate a smooth vacuum spacetime? A similar question applies to the spacetimes constructed by numerical relativity.

accepted.question_text: Can one devise a reasonable numerical-relativity evolution scheme that preserves the Einstein constraint equations and can serve as a step toward proving convergence of a numerical scheme to a long-time solution of the Einstein equations?

evidence.quote: Devise a reasonable scheme which can be shown to preserve the constraints (cf. [DS]). This may also be thought of as a step towards showing convergence of some numerical scheme to a (long time) solution of the Einstein equations.

accepted.question_text: Can one prove a uniqueness theorem for maximal surfaces under only the dominant energy condition, filling the gap between known uniqueness under the timelike convergence condition and uniqueness in spacetimes with a timelike Killing vector?

evidence.quote: Maximal Cauchy surfaces are known to be unique if the timelike convergence condition (TCC) is satisfied [BF,COMB], or if the spacetime admits a timelike Killing vector. There is an unsatisfactory gap between these two conditions, which includes the dominant energy condition. Prove a uniqueness theorem for maximal surfaces, assuming only DE.

accepted.question_text: Can the elliptic estimates for maximal and constant-mean-curvature hypersurfaces be generalized to prove existence of a constant-mean-curvature hypersurface asymptotic to a prescribed cut of future null infinity in an asymptotically flat spacetime, and what are the weakest asymptotic assumptions on future null infinity for this result?

evidence.quote: Generalise the estimates of [BRl] to show the existence of a CMC hypersurface asymptotic to a given cut of ~+ in an AF spacetime. What are the weakest asymptotic conditions on ~ + for which this holds?

accepted.question_text: If V is an asymptotically flat spacetime with a Cauchy surface that has no horizons, must V contain a maximal Cauchy hypersurface?

evidence.quote: Let V be an AF spacetime, having a Cauchy surface without horizons. Show there is a maximal Cauchy hypersurface in V.

accepted.question_text: In a boost-type domain, must every maximal surface be asymptotically flat and coincide with the maximal slices constructed by earlier boost-problem methods?

evidence.quote: Show that a maximal surface in a boost-type domain [COM] is necessarily AF and must coincide with the maximal slices which can be constructed by [BRl; COMB].

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a timelike geodesically complete, inextendible Lorentz manifold satisfying an energy condition and having a partial Cauchy surface that contains a trapped surface?

evidence.quote: Is there a timelike geodesically complete, inextendible Lorentz manifold satisfying an energy condition and having a partial Cauchy surface which contains a trapped surface?

accepted.question_text: Can a weak Cauchy surface, defined as a pointwise limit of Cauchy surfaces, in a globally hyperbolic spacetime satisfying suitable energy conditions contain an inextendible null geodesic?

evidence.quote: Show that a weak Cauchy surface (i.e. a pointwise limit of a sequence of Cauchy surfaces) in a globally hyperbolic spacetime satisfying suitable energy conditions, cannot contain an inextendible null geodesic.

accepted.question_text: If a spacetime satisfies condition (G) when some point has a domain of influence meeting every inextendible timelike curve, does failure of condition (G), or the presence of a hidden infinity, in a cosmological spacetime satisfying the timelike convergence condition force a trapped surface and thereby support the dichotomy that the spacetime is either timelike geodesically incomplete or splits isometrically as R x M?

evidence.quote: A spacetime satisfies condition (G) if there is a point whose domain of influence meets every inextendible timelike curve [Gel;Gal;BR5]. Show that if condition (G) fails or there is a "hidden infinity" [BR5] in a cosmological spacetime V satisfying TCC, then there is a trapped surface in V. This would give a proof of Conjecture: Let V be a cosmological spacetime satisfying the timelike convergence condition, Then either V is timelike geodesically incomplete or V splits as IRxM isometrically (and thus Vis static).

accepted.question_text: Can one prove a singularity theorem using the dominant energy condition rather than the timelike convergence condition?

evidence.quote: Prove a singularity theorem assuming the dominant energy condition rather than the timelike convergence condition. The DE condition is the most natural energy condition from a physical standpoint [HE], but unfortunately TCC seems to be the most useful from the standpoint of proving singularity theorems.

accepted.question_text: For low-regularity Lorentzian metrics, such as continuous or Holder-continuous metrics for which length-maximizing timelike curves exist, is a maximizing geodesic unique; what physical interpretation should be given to non-uniqueness of the geodesic initial value problem; and should such a metric be regarded as singular?

evidence.quote: However, length maximising timelike curves will exist if the metric is merely co, and these will be o,a (O<a.<l) if the metric is co,a. Is a maximising geodesic unique in this case? Is there a physical interpretation of non-uniqueness of the IVP? In particular, should a metric for which uniqueness fails for the IVP for timelike geodesics, be considered singular?

accepted.question_text: Can one prove a long-time existence theorem for the vacuum asymptotically flat Einstein equations in the maximal slicing gauge, beyond the nearly flat small-data case?

evidence.quote: Show a long~time existence theorem for the vacuum AF Einstein equations in the maximal slicing gauge [ME]. For nearly flat initial data this is major work of Christodoulou-Klainerman [CK2].

accepted.question_text: What conditions on asymptotically flat initial data guarantee that the null infinity of the resulting Einstein initial-value-problem solution is regular enough for the Penrose extended manifold to exist with at least a C3 metric, so that the peeling theorem holds?

evidence.quote: Determine conditions on AF initial data which ensure that the null infinity of the resulting solution of the IVP is sufficiently regular that the Penrose extended manifold exists, with at least C3 metric so the peeling theorem holds [PRl].

accepted.question_text: Does there exist an exact purely radiative vacuum Einstein spacetime with complete smooth future and past null infinity, regular timelike infinities, and positive mass?

evidence.quote: Give an exact "purely radiative spacetime", i.e. a solution to the Einstein vacuum equations which has complete smooth ~±, regular i±, and positive mass, or show the existence of such a spacetime.

accepted.question_text: What is the weakest regularity under which a vacuum metric can satisfy the Einstein vacuum equations, and how should one determine the optimal coordinates or best differentiable structure for such a low-regularity metric?

evidence.quote: Find the weakest possible regularity for a vacuum metric [CC;HKM;KT]. As observed by G. Huisken, the Ricci tensor is defined distributionally when the metric satisfies merely g,g-le L00 , Clge L2, so a metric satisfying only these regularity conditions could conceivably satisfy the (distributional) vacuum Einstein equations.

accepted.question_text: Are there regularity conditions for the vacuum Einstein initial value problem that guarantee existence but not uniqueness of a globally hyperbolic spacetime, and is there smooth initial data whose vacuum evolution develops a singularity that admits non-unique globally hyperbolic extensions?

evidence.quote: By analogy with the IVP for geodesics, there may be regularity conditions for the vacuum Einstein IVP which guarantee existence of a solution, but not uniqueness [CBY] (see the previous question). Should such a (globally hyperbolic!) spacetime be considered singular? Is there an example of (smooth) initial data whose vacuum evolution develops a singularity, but which can be extended, non-uniquely but still satisfying global hyperbolicity, beyond this singularity?

accepted.question_text: Can one prove long-time existence, as the trace of the extrinsic curvature tends to plus or minus infinity, for the cosmological vacuum Einstein equations in constant-mean-curvature slicing gauge?

evidence.quote: Show long-time (trK-1-±oo) existence in the CMC slicing gauge for the cosmological spacetime vacuum equations (this is the compact Cauchy surface version of a previous question).

accepted.question_text: Does every globally hyperbolic, maximally extended solution of the Einstein or Einstein-Maxwell equations on V = R x S3 contain a maximal hypersurface and both a big bang and a big crunch; equivalently, are there vacuum or Einstein-Maxwell solutions on R x S3 that cannot be foliated by constant-mean-curvature hypersurfaces, even in the spatially homogeneous Bianchi IX case?

evidence.quote: Prove that every globally hyperbolic, maximally extended spacetime solution of the Einstein o:r Einstein-Maxwell equations on V = RxS3 contains a maximal hype:rsurface (and also both a big bang and big crunch). Are there any vacuum or Einstein-Maxwell solutions on Rx83 which cannot be foliated by CMC hypersurfaces? (This is a restatement of the previous question). Special case: Prove this result for the spatially homogeneous solutions (Bianchi IX) .

accepted.question_text: In an appropriate sense, is the set of spacetime metrics that can be smoothly or distributionally extended across Cauchy horizons a measure-zero subset of all spacetimes?

evidence.quote: Show that, in an appropriate sense, the set of spacetime metrics which are (smoothly?, distributionally?) extendible across Cauchy horizons are "measure zero" in the set of all spacetimes ([ME;Ml], generally asked about spacetimes with compact Cauchy surfaces).

accepted.question_text: Can one find an exact solution of the Einstein equations representing two orbiting bodies, and is the two-body system unstable in Einstein gravity?

evidence.quote: Fi.nd an exact solution of the Einstein equations which represents two orbiting bodies. Is the 2-body system unstable in Einstein gravity?

accepted.question_text: Which spacetimes are asymptotically velocity dominated near a singularity, under an appropriate definition of that asymptotic behavior?

evidence.quote: Determine the class of spacetinnes which are, in an appropriately defined sense, asymptotically velocity dominated near the singularity [BKL;ELS].

accepted.question_text: Can one prove that the only solution of the vacuum Robinson-Trautman equations on S2 x R with positive mass is the Schwarzschild metric, and can an analogous theorem be proved for the Einstein-Maxwell Robinson-Trautman equations?

evidence.quote: Show that the only solution of the vacuum Robinson-Trautman equations on S2xR with mass > 0, is the Schwarzschild metric [RA;SB2;LPPS]. Can a similar theorem for the Einstein-Maxwell RT equations be shown?

accepted.question_text: Can one prove that perturbations of the Schwarzschild and Kerr black-hole solutions decay, as suggested by physical and linearized arguments, thereby establishing black-hole stability in that sense?

evidence.quote: Physical and linearisation arguments suggest that a perturbation of the Schwarzscrilld (and Kerr) solution decays exponentially (black holes a:re stable); see Chandresekhar [Ch] for a comprehensive review. Prove this.

accepted.question_text: If a cosmological spacetime has constant-mean-curvature initial data with positive Ricci 3-curvature, does the Einstein evolution preserve positivity of the Ricci curvature?

evidence.quote: Show that a cosmological spacetime with CMC initial data having positive Ricci 3-curvature, has an evolution which preserves Ricci positivity (S.T. Yau).

accepted.question_text: Can one define a sensible quasi-local mass that appears in nontrivial theorems, for example a theorem asserting that if a three-dimensional region of volume V has quasi-local mass at least a threshold M0 depending on V and other data, then every spacetime containing that region must contain a trapped surface and hence a black hole?

evidence.quote: Find a sensible notion of quasi-local mass which appears in non-trivial theorems such as; If a 3-dimensional region with volume V has QL-mass ;::: M 0 (V, ... ), then any spacetime containing this region must have a trapped surface and thus a black hole.

accepted.question_text: Does the class of asymptotically flat 3-manifolds satisfying the hypotheses of the positive mass theorem have a weak compactness property, such as subsequential convergence for sequences with bounded mass and bounded geometry, and what regularity should the limiting manifold have?

evidence.quote: Show the set 'f 'JTI, of AF 3-manifolds which satisfy the conditions of the positive mass theorem [SY1,2;WE] has some weak compactness property, eg. a sequence {Mk} with bounded mass and bounded geometry has a convergent subsequence (cf. [0M2] and these proceedings). What regularity might we expect in the limit manifold?

accepted.question_text: Given a bounded region Q with connected boundary inside an asymptotically flat 3-manifold satisfying the positive mass theorem conditions, can one find an isometric extension that is static outside Q and has least ADM mass among all no-horizon extensions of Q?

evidence.quote: Let Q c (M,g) be a bounded region in a 'f 'JTI, manifold, with connected boundary. Show there is another 'f 'l1'b manifold (M* ,g*) ::> Q, isometrically, such that (M*,g*) is static outside 0 (cf. [CW]). This is part of the static metric conjecture of [BR6], which further conjectures that (M* ,g*) has least ADM mass amongst all those 'f 'JTI, extensions of Q having no horizon outside Q.

accepted.question_text: Can one prove the positive mass theorem using Geroch's idea of foliating by 2-spheres, including proving the existence of foliations with the required special properties?

evidence.quote: Construct a proof of the positive mass theorem, based on Ge:roch's foliation by 2-spheres idea [Ge2]. There are several variations of this argument [JK;JP; LV2], but these aU :require the existence of a foliation with special properties-the (highly non-trivial) problem then being that of showing the existence of such foliations.

accepted.question_text: Is the Bartnik quasi-local mass strictly positive for non-flat data, and is the Penrose quasi-local mass non-negative on reasonable data?

evidence.quote: Show the Bartnik quasi-local mass [BR6] is strictly positive for non-flat data. Show that the Penrose quasi-local mass is non-negative on reasonable data (there are examples [TP] with negative mass).

accepted.question_text: How are the various definitions of quasi-local mass related to one another?

evidence.quote: Explain the relation between the various definitions of quasi-local mass.
